title: Incident retrospective: NAT/masquerade rule loss during Private VPC orchestrator rollout
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: During a staged control-plane upgrade for Private/VPC fleets on 2025-02-11 we observed a subset of customer nodes lose outbound SNAT/MASQUERADE rules. The lost rules caused intermittent API-server connectivity timeouts for several on-prem tenants and led to degraded routing for runtime sidecars. Impact window: ~23 minutes for the worst-affected fleets and increased API error rates for ~120 tenants (pilot/private customers). This ticket captures the retrospective analysis, immediate mitigations, and durable action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-11 09:08 UTC - Automated alert: control-plane health checks show >50% API latency increase for private region eu-west-1-prv-2
2025-02-11 09:12 UTC - On-call (Marco) escalated to networking and private ops. Initial hypothesis: control-plane load spike during rollout
2025-02-11 09:20 UTC - Observed kube-proxy logs with frequent iptables restore warnings and missing MASQUERADE chain entries on affected nodes

2025-02-11 09:28 UTC - Mitigation: paused the orchestrator upgrade, rolled back the latest AMI changes for the next batch, and re-applied iptables rules via emergency runbook (netops script iptables-restore + verify), partial recovery began by 09:31 UTC
2025-02-11 09:35 UTC - Full connectivity restored for most tenants after reapplying rules; continued monitoring and manual remediation for straggler nodes until 09:45 UTC
2025-02-11 10:00 UTC - Post-incident teleconference initiated; agreed to create this retrospective and track permanent fixes
root_cause: An upgrade step that rebuilt network namespaces and refreshed node-side network tools executed an iptables-save/restore flow that unintentionally dropped runtime-generated MASQUERADE rules. The change in the AMI image included an init script ordering change (iptables-restore executed before the sidecar reconciler), combined with a timing window where the orchestrator replaced host networking components. The deployment lacked a preflight verification for reachable kernel netfilter state and a canary gate that validates preservation of transient NAT chains.
mitigation_summary: Immediate rollback of the AMI across the pending batch, reapplication of MASQUERADE rules via netops emergency script, and pausing of the orchestrator rollout. Added a short-term monitoring rule to alert when MASQUERADE chain length deviates by >25% from baseline per-node.
action_items: ENG-42219-A1: Update upgrade orchestration to persist and restore runtime NAT chains atomically; implement iptables-save/restore wrapper that preserves existing MASQUERADE entries (owner: Marco Santos, due: 2025-02-28)
ENG-42219-A2: Add a preflight check in the canary pipeline that verifies iptables chain existence and conntrack stats before marking canary healthy (owner: NetOps - Priya Desai, due: 2025-02-25)

ENG-42219-A3: Implement an automated test in CI that simulates replacement of host networking components and asserts MASQUERADE persistence (owner: Infra QA - Daniel Lee, estimate: 5 pts, due: 2025-03-05)
ENG-42219-A4: Add a dashboard and PagerDuty alert for sudden drops in MASQUERADE chain length and per-node conntrack table churn (owner: Observability - Mei Chen, due: 2025-02-24)
ENG-42219-A5: Document runbook for rapid reapplication of NAT rules and include validated iptables-restore artifact in private runbook (owner: Private Ops - Samira Patel, due: 2025-02-18)

notes: We saw the largest customer impact for tenants with long-lived sidecar connections that assume stable SNAT mappings.
This incident exposed a brittle dependency between AMI init ordering and runtime reconciler behavior; plan to harden the boundary with explicit preservation APIs.
Security review not required for the immediate fixes but any AMI change that touches network tooling must run through the private AMI checklist going forward.
